newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary APV scandal report fails to find initiator.
newsitem.headline: Hungary APV scandal report fails to find initiator.

text.p: An investigation into irregular payments to a consultant which led to the sacking of the minister in charge of Hungary's privatisation agency, plus the entire board, has failed to find out who authorised the work.

The report by APV's supervisory board investigated how consultant Marta Tocsik was paid a 804-million-forint ($5.2 million) success fee for negotiating on APV's behalf payments to local authorities for land on which privatised state companies were based.
After the scandal broke, Prime Minister Gyula Horn dismissed industry and trade minister Tamas Suchman and the whole of the APV executive board.
According to an APV statement released to Hungarian news agency MTI, APV's supervisory board said it was unable to find out who had commissioned Tocsik.
"A verbal decision was made on concluding the contract without a tender prior to the decision by the board accepting the contract, which was enforced by chairman of the board Imre Szokai," it said.

As well as blaming Suchman and the APV board, the report laid special responsibility for the affair upon the legal counsellor dealing in the case, Peter Liszkai, and financial deputy general manager Istvan Kamaras, who both signed the contract with Tocsik.
The report said APV transferred 20.4 billion forints in cash and four billion forints in limited liability holdings and company shares to local councils as compensation for the assets.
A parliamentary committee is looking into the affair while Hungary's Chief Prosecutor has initiated criminal proceedings.
